reason: All four algebraic clauses are covered: endpoint entries and shared-incidence expansion, covariance of independent finite-second-moment effects, general-N role mismatch, and the GLS left-inverse/covariance identity. The GLS statement also applies to symmetric nonsingular indefinite matrices with nonsingular F-transpose C-inverse F; positive definite C and full column rank F imply its guards, so this valid generalization loses no canonical case. The real parameters denote the variance values tau-squared and sigma-squared, rather than their square roots.

The concrete iid sign-pair model, all population and finite sample matrices, rank-failure probability, residual bounds, positive-probability eight-unit atom, joint second-order Gaussian-polynomial limit, strictly positive limiting negative-variance probability, completed-pivot nonnormality, and both consistency statements cover (a)-(d). The zero inverse and pivot completions are disclosed; no hypothesis is assumed to obtain the counterexample. This is the canonical counterexample, not a refutation of Proposition 1.

Under exactly the bounded symmetric iid kernel/projection setting, the statement covers the shared-endpoint identity, possibly singular projection CLT, target limit, sandwich consistency, every positive-variance contrast pivot, nonpositive-variance probability, and nominal coverage for every alpha in (0,1). It also supplies the degenerate-contrast failure example. The pivot is explicitly completed by zero on nonpositive variance events; its normal-limit conclusion has no extra eventual almost-sure positivity assumption. Normal quantiles only use their ordinary domain.

The intercept fair-sign model covers all of (a)-(e), including fixed positive bounded weights, projection/residual/design certificates, geometric identities, exact estimator coefficients and variance, inconsistency and limits, the first-eight-positive event and sandwich separation, nonexistence of any common deterministic target, and the elementwise-finite repeated-record transfer. The directed duplicate realization is also present. Added N<2 identities use explicitly disclosed zero completion; all substantive canonical formulas use N>=2 or N>=8.

The current statement covers strengthened C1 with common record-index kernels, uniformly bounded counts/data, positive limiting normalized design, and the exact scaled overlap-meat condition on block means; C2 for one common ordered kernel and its reversal with at most one record per direction, positive bounded normalized deterministic weights and positive limiting design; C3 ordinary-inverse scale invariance in the standing bounded-data domain; and C4 the bounded-weight obstruction. A deterministic common-record witness additionally shows total-score centering does not replace overlap control. No inverse-moment or extra sample-rank hypothesis is added.
